Shri Nitin Gupta - Government Advocate for the respondent/

Order
This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 seeking anticipatory bail in connection with FIR/Crime No.126/2025 dated 18.02.2025 registered at Police Station Ranjhi, District Jabalpur for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471/34 of IPC.

2. Learned counsel for the applicant contends that the present applicant is working as programmer on contract basis and the allegation against her is that the caste certificates were issued by the present applicant to two persons, namely, Dilip Kumar and Mukesh Barman whereas they were not entitled for the caste certificate.

It is contended by the counsel that the present applicant was working as operator and dispatcher on contractual basis and when the applications are received from the Lok Seva Kendra, they were processed by the computer operator and it is the responsibility of the Sub-Divisional Officer to issue caste certificate.
In the present case also, caste certificates to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12120 2 MCRC-10569-2025 the aforesaid persons were issued by the Sub-Divisional Officer.

It is further contended by the counsel that as per the Circular dated 11.07.2005 issued by the Department of General Administration, it is the bounden duty of the Sub- Divisional Officer to issue caste certificate and even if there is any defect in issuance of the caste certificate, the same can also be cancelled as per the provisions mentioned in the aforesaid guidelines.

It is contended by the counsel that as the caste certificate has undisputedly Smt. Archana Dahiya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130581448/
1 been issued by signature of the Sub-Divisional Officer and there are no allegation of forging of any signature against the present applicant, she deserves to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for the State has opposed the application and submitted that it was the responsibility of the present applicant to produce all applications before the Sub-Divisional Officer and after taking decision from the Sub-Divisional Officer, there should have been a relevant order and after the order, caste certificates have been issued.

sentences.text: However, the present applicant without making entry of the applications in register, misused the digital tokan and the caste certificates were issued.
Thus, looking to the serious allegation against the present applicant, the present application deserves to be dismissed.

4. Heard the rival submissions and perused the case diary.
5.
A perusal of the case diary prima facie reflects that the present applicant was working as computer operator.

The caste certificates which are available in the case diary, issued with the signature of the Sub-Divisional Officer and as per the guidelines dated 11.07.20025, it is the Sub-Divisional NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12120 3 MCRC-10569-2025 Officer,
who can enquire into the eligibility for issuance of caste certificate if in the inquiry the applicant therein is not found entitled for the same.

6. Considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case and also the fact that the present applicant is woman and was only engaged on contractual basis, this Court deems it appropriate to enlarge the applicant on anticipatory bail, therefore, without commenting on the merit of the case, the application is allowed.
7.

It is directed that in the event of arrest, applicant- Smt. Archana Dahiya shall be enlarged on bail on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer for her appearance before him during the course of investigation or before the trial Court concerned during trial, as the case may be.
8. It is further directed that the applicant shall abide by all the conditions as enumerated under Section 482(2) of BNSS.
